why: The hardest form of the shortest valid window with a frequency map: a window is valid when it covers every character of t with multiplicity. Grow right until valid, then shrink left as far as the window stays valid, recording the shortest; track validity with a counter of characters whose need is met so each step is O(1).
hints: Brute force checks every substring. For a fixed right end, if a window is valid, is a longer one ending there valid too?
Yes, so keep need[c] counts from t and a 'missing' counter. Expand right, decreasing need; when missing hits 0, shrink left while the window stays valid.
Record (length, start) while valid and before removing s[left]; prefer the earlier start on ties by only replacing on strictly shorter. O(|s| + |t|).
pitfalls: Multiplicity matters: t = 'aa' needs two a's.
Ties: the earliest start wins, so update only when strictly shorter.
